analysis.title: Chip CDS Flips Wider Than Hyperscalers As Goldman Warns "The Index Is Hiding The Damage"
key_insights: Credit indices barely moved during the tech selloff. CDX IG tightened 0.6bp on the week against almost 3bps of widening implied by its usual beta to the S&P. CDX HY moved 0.3bps against 17bps implied.

On the Thursday S&P drawdown of 4.4%, CDX HY fell 0.75pts versus an equity-implied 1.45pts, a 2.7-sigma outlier per Goldman lev fin strategist KC O'Connor. For the week, IG ended 1bp wider and HY 4bps tighter.

Goldman's Alisha Pasi says the index hides damage in AI and energy. The average HY AI bond traded at GS fell 1.67pts last week versus a 0.36pt gain across the rest of HY. Energy widened 24bps while broader HY tightened 4bps.
CoreWeave's 8.5% 2032 bonds ended the week at 71.0, down 8.5 points, the worst performer in Goldman's European distressed wrap. CoreWeave reports Tuesday.
AI bond supply is shifting to shorter duration. META sold only $2.75bn of 30yr bonds in a $15bn deal and brought no 40yr for the first time. ORCL's $10bn deal had no 30yr or 40yr.
Goldman's 30-year hyperscaler basket flattened against its 10-year basket by about 25%, from 40bps to 31bps, while the non-AI 10s30s curve barely moved in three months.
Meta's $15bn compared with $25bn-plus the Street expected. Goldman's Brad Shelofsky said Microsoft, Oracle and Meta deals underwhelmed in size and duration versus expectations.
Goldman's total return swap (TRS) book leans about 3.5:1 short, with an overwhelming bias toward 30y IG spread shorts, the part of the curve hyperscalers just stopped supplying.

A basket of chip CDS now trades wider than a basket of hyperscaler CDS for the first time in three months. McCarthy attributes this to expected growth in chip financing as a share of AI issuance in 2027.

In the week to Nov 5, Intel CDS widened 40bps, AMD 26.5bps and Broadcom 17.6bps, the three biggest wideners in CDX IG. AI CDS volume ran $8-10 billion per week over the past two weeks, the most active ever excluding the September roll.

Goldman's Sarah Zappone describes SPV-backed AI issuance as a structural shift. Bonds are issued by a PE sponsor's vehicle while the hyperscaler is the tenant paying the lease. Roughly $150bn is announced for next year against a roughly $900mm market today, which the author puts at about 165 times the existing market.

The SPV paper is shorter, amortizing, usually secured, sometimes backed by a hyperscaler residual value guarantee, and pays over 100bps above comparable unsecured debt. The flagship deal has no public ratings. Zappone warns it could compete for capital with HY.

Goldman's Alec Phillips said midterm wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio mean up to around 40% of planned data center capacity is impacted, likely through a moratorium lasting several months. Goldman Research raised its 2026/27 data center construction forecasts and introduced $125bn for 2028, arguing restrictions stretch the cycle rather than shrink the TAM.
Shelofsky expects high quality hyperscalers to outperform neoclouds and AI equipment suppliers, since neocloud debt servicing depends on delivery, and says it is paid to sell those rallies.

Brian Garrett's vol panic index hit 9.57 on Thursday, a level that has historically been a good buying opportunity. He sees a violent positioning reset, not a systemic event. US fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 1st percentile.

Tony Pasquariello says the market absorbed a huge risk transfer from the trading community alongside a buyers' strike. He expects 2027 to bring the largest increase in net supply since 2000 and says the AI buildout is at more risk than at any point in the past four years. His TMT momentum pair has lost two-thirds of its value since June.
Goldman strategists see USD IG above 93bp and HY above 335bp into early December. Friday's 165K payrolls put a December hike back on the table.

The author's view is that the index stayed calm because risk moved into leases, vendor guarantees, SPVs, chipmakers and neoclouds, and that dispersion matters once one of those slices misses a payment.

market_movers.rationale: CoreWeave's 8.5% 2032 bonds fell 8.5 points to 71.0 on the week, the worst in Goldman's European distressed wrap. The company reports Tuesday.
Intel 5-year CDS widened 40bps in the week to Nov 5, the largest widening in CDX IG.
AMD CDS widened 26.5bps in the week to Nov 5 and trades at 150bps versus a two-month tight of 95bps.
Broadcom CDS widened 17.6bps to 195bps (two-month tight 125bps). The vendor guaranteed most of its record AI debt deal.
Oracle CDS is at 310bps versus a two-month tight of 205bps, the widest among hyperscalers. Its $10bn deal had no 30yr or 40yr tranche.
Nvidia CDS at 140bps versus a two-month tight of 90bps as chip credits widen.
Meta sold $15bn of bonds against $25bn-plus expected, with only $2.75bn of 30yr and no 40yr tranche. CDS is at 110bps.
Nebius reports Thursday and is grouped with neoclouds that face delivery-linked debt servicing risk.

sector_views.rationale: Shelofsky expects them to underperform high quality hyperscalers because debt servicing depends on delivery and data center moratorium delays. He says it is paid to sell those rallies.
Shelofsky expects high quality hyperscalers to outperform neoclouds and AI suppliers. Microsoft CDS sits at its two-month tights at 50bps.
Energy HY spreads widened 24bps while the broader HY index tightened 4bps.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave reports Tuesday and Nebius reports Thursday. Rich Privorotsky says these matter more for underlying AI sentiment than the weekend's Jensen Huang headlines.

Goldman Research raised 2026 data center construction forecast to $100 billion from $87 billion and 2027 to $80 billion from $67 billion, per the text, and introduced $125 billion for 2028. The source text is garbled on which figure belongs to which year.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Described as a blowout that put a December hike back on the table.
Index tightened against about 3bps of widening implied by its beta to the S&P.
Index moved far less than equity beta implied.

trade_ideas.description: Sell rallies in neoclouds and AI equipment suppliers relative to high quality hyperscalers
trade_ideas.rationale: Neocloud debt servicing is predicated on delivery, which is exposed to data center moratorium delays.

risk_factors: Data center moratorium delays could affect up to around 40% of planned capacity and delay debt servicing for borrowers tied to delivery.
Net supply in 2027 is expected to be the largest increase since 2000.
SPV-backed AI financing has no public ratings, an unclear draw schedule and limited data room access, and its issuance could compete for capital with HY.
Off-balance sheet hyperscaler commitments of $3.6 trillion per Goldman, or $4.1 trillion per the author.
A missed payment on one of the SPV, lease or vendor-guaranteed slices could end the dispersion-only regime.
A buyers' strike persists despite washed-out positioning.
Payrolls strength puts a December hike back on the table.
charts_described: CDX IG and CDX HY actual weekly moves versus S&P-implied moves: IG tightened 0.6bp against almost 3bps implied, HY moved 0.3bps against 17bps implied.
Goldman's 30-year hyperscaler basket versus 10-year basket flattened from 40bps to 31bps, against a non-AI 10s30s curve that barely moved in three months.
Intel, AMD and Broadcom CDS were the three biggest wideners in CDX IG in the week to Nov 5.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and the S&P 4.4% on Thursday, the worst day for tech since Covid. CDX IG widened 3.5 basis points that day.
Brian Garrett's vol panic index reached 9.57 on Thursday. Readings above 9 have historically been a good buying opportunity. He sees a violent positioning reset, not a systemic event.
US fundamental long/short net leverage is at the 1st percentile.
Hedge funds have sold since mid-August, households turned down late in the summer and buybacks have been constrained.
Goldman's TRS book leans about 3.5:1 short with a bias toward 30y IG spread shorts.
Pasquariello's TMT momentum pair has lost two-thirds of its value since June.
geopolitical: Midterm election wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio led to data center restrictions. Goldman's Alec Phillips said up to around 40% of planned capacity could be impacted by a moratorium lasting several months.
Out of 45 data center votes across America, exactly one went the industry's way.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Garrett sees a violent positioning reset rather than a systemic event, with a vol panic index of 9.57 historically a buying signal. Hyperscalers are high quality and Goldman sees the data center delay stretching the cycle rather than shrinking the TAM.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk has moved into chip CDS, SPVs, vendor guarantees and neoclouds. Pasquariello says the AI buildout is at more risk than at any point in the past four years, and 2027 net supply is expected to be the largest increase since 2000.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A missed payment on one of the SPV, lease or vendor-guaranteed slices would end the calm dispersion, per the author. Goldman's bull case relies on a December supply lull to help its IG 93bp and HY 335bp targets.

theme_stances.key_argument: The index stayed calm because AI risk moved into leases, vendor guarantees, SPVs, chipmakers and neoclouds that the index does not capture.
theme_stances.evidence: The index is hiding the damage
